title: Is the sales pipeline the binding constraint?
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: Whether meetings, proposals, win rate, no-decision losses or the owner's selling time limit growth, and whether more outreach would help or feed a leak.
applies_when: Owner wants more leads or to hire a seller
exclusions: Self-serve purchase with no sales step
required_inputs: Meetings booked and held, proposals, won, lost, no-decision, unqualified, over a period
evidence_requirements: per period: meetings booked, meetings held, proposals/quotes sent, won, lost, unqualified, average won value
owner selling hours per week and maximum meetings the owner can hold
customers won through the owner's own conversations
price and margin for value per meeting
owner hours per week available for selling
founder win rate per held meeting over enough decisions
average deal value and cycle length
owner time split (prospecting vs selling vs delivery)
closed opportunities coded won / lost-to-competitor / no decision / disqualified
named customers and their revenue share
support and integration hours per customer
missing_data_behavior: Fewer than about 5 decided deals: counts only, verdict unknown.
No prior period or target: no verdict (no reliable external sales benchmarks).

decision_branches.if: Win rate falling or calendar full
decision_branches.then: Don't add outreach; fix qualification, proposal or capacity.
Treat 'do nothing' as the main rival; pitch and proposal work.

implementation_steps: Count stages over a fixed window (code).
Compute hold rate, held->proposal, proposal->won, win per held meeting, unqualified share, median days to close (code).
Compare to the owner's own prior period or stated target; external benchmarks only as grade-D context, never as a verdict.
Name the weakest link and its competing explanation.
Daily hygiene: uncovered deals, late-stage deals untouched 7+ days, deals stuck past the owner's typical stage time, past-due next steps.
Prioritise follow-up from closest-to-money down, by value.
Confirm price fit for human selling
Compute expected bookings per seller = meetings per month x win rate x deal value (code).
Compute cost of sales = seller cost / bookings (code).
Compare against owner's margin room, not a generic band.
Compute no-decision share and decided win rate
Name the status quo alternative explicitly
List customers with revenue and support hours.
Compute revenue and support share per customer.
Document sales stages and conversion after the first few deals.
dependencies: Stage definitions with entry criteria the owner agrees to
At least a few closed decisions; otherwise use per-deal review, not rates
a price that pays for human selling (BRP-19 / scoring.ts LOW_TICKET_USD_MONTH)
Retention evidence that won clients get value (K7)
a record of recent deals (even a short list from the owner)

cash_and_labor_requirements.labor: minutes per week to keep stages true
cash_and_labor_requirements.capability: CRM stages with dates; deterministic aggregation

metrics: win rate per held first meeting
pipeline value (open, unweighted) and won value
ramp time to founder-level win rate
time to first value against client baseline
guardrails: Book win-rate and show-rate figures are dated venture-SaaS context, never verdicts.
Few accounts means research is a census, not a sample.
Benchmarks from this book are grade D and dated
Owner time is priced into CAC (cacFull)
No promise of results from hiring
Book salary and cost-of-sales bands are dated US venture-SaaS context, grade D
Employment law and contractor rules vary (external)
Reported 40-60% is a cited, dated B2B figure, not a reference range for diagnosis (base-rates.md rule)
no customer named publicly without permission
alternatives_when_constrained: No CRM data: ask the owner for the six counts for the last 60-90 days
Very low volume: qualitative review of the last 5 won and 5 lost deals
No owner time: PB-referrals or PB-partners
Can't afford a hire: freelance appointment setter on a trial, partners/referrals, or raise price to free founder time (PB-capacity, PB-price-increase)
No deal history: ask the owner for the last 5 that didn't buy and why
no CRM: owner's spreadsheet of deals and hours
stop_conditions: Re-diagnose each month or after 10 new closed decisions
If the named constraint does not move after one cycle of fixes, test the competing explanation
After about 20 qualified conversations with no win, review ICP and offer (PB-interviews) before adding volume
If a new seller's win rate stays well below founder level after a set ramp, review onboarding before hiring more
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Stage labels that describe seller activity instead of buyer progress
Using CRM default stage probabilities as forecasts
The owner hires a rep from a bigger competitor too early: that rep sells to old contacts and can't diagnose why prospects say no
Premature scaling: hiring sales to 'figure it out'
Lagged scaling: founder keeps closing when the motion is proven
Reading no decision as 'they like their current tool'
Pitching the future vision so buyers wait
Self-serve SMB SaaS behaves more like consumer funnels.
Enterprise case-study requests can breach confidentiality; owner approval needed.

missing_prerequisite.rule: proposed: For sales-led businesses, diagnosis reads a sales block (booked, held, proposals, won, lost, unqualified, value, owner meeting capacity) and names the weakest link in code.
proposed: PB-cold-outreach requires owner selling hours (hours_min about 3 a week) as well as price and mailbox.
proposed: add an optional deal-outcome breakdown to owner inputs; compute no-decision share deterministically

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: Do not recommend more top-of-funnel outreach when win rate per held meeting is below the owner's own target or prior period, unless the owner's calendar is empty and sample size is adequate.
proposed: When the owner's meeting capacity is >=80% used and win rate is falling, name selling capacity (delivery) as the constraint.
proposed: Fewer than 5 closed decisions in the window => rates reported as counts with 'too few to judge'.
proposed: The first sales hire targets the step that limits the owner's selling time (prospecting, selling or delivery), computed from the owner's time split.
proposed: never use the book's 40-60% as a reference range in diagnosis
proposed: for B2B types with fewer than about 30 customers, diagnosis readings report counts, not rates, and experiment lints block significance-style tests (route to interviews or before/after).

unknown_to_investigate.rule: proposed: Kazanjy's 15-30% win-rate band may be shown only as 'author view, 2020, venture SaaS, grade D'; it never sets a weak/ok verdict.

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: when the owner reports no customers won through personal conversations, plans must not lead with hiring a salesperson, outsourced SDR or appointment-setting agency; lead with owner-run outreach, warm intros or inbound capture.
proposed: Do not recommend hiring a salesperson until the owner has a stable win rate over enough closed decisions and evidence won clients succeed.
proposed: when one customer exceeds a large share of revenue (owner-defined), the plan includes a disentanglement step before scale.

economic_feasibility.rule: proposed: Hiring recommendations show expected bookings and cost of sales computed from the owner's own rates, with ramp time stated as an assumption.

reconciliation_note: No sales stage exists in diagnosis today (backlog CG-09, CG-10).
